notes.headline: Data Center REITs — EQIX, DLR: real-estate arbitrage on AI scarcity, 50-year lease durability.

interconnect_reits.label: Interconnect / Hyperscaler Co-Lo
interconnect_reits.thesis: EQIX Q1 2026 $2.44B (+9.8%), 60% of largest deals AI-related, AFFO guide $4.20-4.28B. DLR signed largest 200MW AI lease in company history, raised capex by $250M to $3.5-4.0B, 1.2GW pipeline (+60%). Northern Virginia, Oregon, Texas command 15-20% power premiums.

diversified_reits.label: Diversified — Data Storage Pivot
diversified_reits.thesis: Iron Mountain ~30% revenue transitioning to data centers from records storage. Less pure-play but more conservative valuation.

lead_lag.horizon: 20-30 year lease durability; 8-9% dividend yields provide downside
lead_lag.chain_flow: Hyperscaler GPU demand → DC capacity shortage → REIT power premium → 20yr leases lock in

notes.thesis: REITs capture the real-estate arbitrage on AI data center scarcity. Power-constrained DCs in Northern Virginia/Oregon/Texas earn 15-20% premiums. EQIX/DLR have 50%+ TAM lock-in through 2028 via 20-30 year lease terms.
caveats: Interest rate sensitivity — REITs underperform when 10yr yields rise sharply.
Power interconnection queue delays could push out new builds (5+ years in PJM).
Hyperscalers building their own DCs (Microsoft) is the long-term competitive risk.
notes.source: Research synthesis — May 2026 + Q1 2026 ER prints

notes.headline: Cooling/Thermal Layer — VRT, MOD: liquid cooling adoption driving 30-40% CAGR.

liquid_cooling.label: Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC)
liquid_cooling.thesis: VRT pure-play DLC leader, NVIDIA GB200 co-design, 3+ year backlog. MOD data center cooling fiscal Q3 +31% sequential, expects $400M+ quarterly, 50-70% growth over next 2 years. SMCI's 70% DLC market share drives this.

air_handling.label: Specialized Air Handling
air_handling.thesis: Specialized HVAC for data center thermal. Less direct AI exposure but real-estate adjacency.

diversified_hvac.label: Diversified Building / HVAC
diversified_hvac.thesis: Johnson Controls — building efficiency. AI is minor revenue contributor; broader cyclical name.

lead_lag.horizon: 3-5 years as DLC adoption ramps from <10% to 50%+ of new DC builds
lead_lag.chain_flow: GPU rack power density (130kW+) → air cooling fails → DLC mandatory → VRT/MOD orderbook

notes.thesis: Liquid cooling adoption is forced by GPU thermal density. SMCI 70% DLC share validates the inflection. MOD's 50-70% growth guidance reflects supply-demand inversion — water scarcity in California/Texas is accelerating adoption further.
caveats: MOD is a small/mid cap with higher vol than VRT.
Hyperscalers may bring some cooling in-house long-term.
Water scarcity could ironically slow adoption if regulators restrict water-cooled designs.

notes.headline: Copper Supercycle — FCX, SCCO: structural 2026-2040 demand from AI DCs + EVs + grid.

majors.label: Copper Majors
majors.thesis: FCX +40% YoY, Grasberg restoration 2027+, largest liquid copper play. SCCO 2026 revenue target $16B (+17%), record 2025 $13.42B. Spot $14.5K/tonne early 2026, consensus $20K+ by 2028-2029.

polymetallic.label: Polymetallic / Hedged
polymetallic.thesis: TECK copper+zinc+coal Chilean expansion. ERO high-grade Brazilian operations, lower permitting risk.

lead_lag.horizon: 10-15 year supercycle; 5% major deposits last decade; 15-17 year permitting lead time
lead_lag.chain_flow: AI DC (50K tonnes/facility) + EV adoption + grid expansion → 50% demand growth → supply-constrained → spot $14.5K → $20K+

notes.thesis: Copper is the single most underappreciated AI-adjacent supercycle. Each AI data center consumes 50,000 tonnes of copper. Combined with EV and grid expansion, demand grows 50% by 2030. Supply is structurally constrained — only 5% of major deposits discovered in the last decade, 15-17 year permitting lead times.
caveats: Cyclical macro exposure — global recession would dent demand near-term despite structural setup.
Grasberg/Chilean political risk (resource nationalism).
Copper trades on China sentiment — any Chinese stimulus disappointment hits the basket.

notes.headline: AI Software/Apps — MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN: $725B 2026 hyperscaler capex driving cloud AI TAM.

hyperscalers.label: Hyperscaler Cloud + AI
hyperscalers.thesis: Combined 2026 capex $575B+ ($200B AMZN, $185B GOOGL, $125B META, $65B MSFT). 75% allocated to AI. AMZN AWS highest growth in 15 quarters, Anthropic partnership. GOOGL Cloud +63% YoY. META core ad +33% (fastest in years). MSFT Azure AI $37B ARR but Q1 2026 was 3rd consecutive miss.

enterprise_ai_apps.label: Enterprise AI Software
enterprise_ai_apps.thesis: PLTR Q1 2026 $1.63B (+85%), record profit, government AI fastest-growing. NOW workflow automation. CRM Einstein 20-25% growth. SNOW data + AI analytics. PLTR is the breakout name.

lead_lag.horizon: Capex cliff risk 2028-2029 if AI revenue doesn't justify spend
lead_lag.chain_flow: AI compute capex → cloud AI TAM expansion → enterprise app monetization → margin proof or capex cut

notes.thesis: Hyperscaler capex of $725B in 2026 (+77% YoY) drives the entire AI infrastructure stack. AI is now 1.2% of US GDP. PLTR is the standout enterprise AI breakout. The risk: if capex doesn't translate to AI revenue by 2028, the cliff is severe.
caveats: MSFT is now a relative laggard — three consecutive quarter misses on Azure.
Open-source LLAMA is commoditizing inference — pressure on proprietary model moats.
Capex-to-revenue conversion is the make-or-break metric — watch quarterly AI revenue disclosures.
PLTR valuation is rich; multiple compression risk if growth slows.

notes.headline: Defense Supercycle — LMT, RTX, NOC + drones: $526B combined backlog, AI/autonomous +15% YoY.

primes.label: Defense Primes
primes.thesis: LMT $179B record backlog, F-35 stabilized. RTX $251B order book — largest in defense. NOC $96B record backlog, naval + electronic warfare. Combined backlog $526B = 3+ years revenue visibility.

drones_autonomy.label: Drones & Autonomous Systems
drones_autonomy.thesis: AVAV drone leader, Ukraine validated. KTOS defense automation + satellite/autonomous platforms. AI/autonomous segment growing 15%+ YoY vs <5% for legacy platforms.

naval_land.label: Naval / Land Systems
naval_land.thesis: Submarines, armored vehicles, combat systems integrating AI. More cyclical than primes.

space_isr.label: Space ISR / Dual-Use Intelligence
space_isr.thesis: BlackSky (BKSY) and Spire Global (SPIR) represent the commercial space intelligence layer that DoD is actively scaling as a cost-efficient alternative to classified satellite programs. BKSY operates a constellation of high-revisit optical satellites — tasked by DoD/NGA for real-time ISR. SPIR provides RF/weather data from 100+ LEO satellites. Both operate on recurring government contracts and benefit directly from the Defense Supercycle: defense ISR budgets growing with autonomous battlefield awareness demand, and Ukraine proving the operational value of commercial satellite intelligence. Fastest-growing segment within defense ISR — higher beta than primes, episodic move potential on contract wins.

lead_lag.horizon: 5-10 year defense cycle; bipartisan support guarantees budget through 2030
lead_lag.chain_flow: Geopolitical escalation → bipartisan budget support → backlog accumulation → autonomous/AI segment + space ISR outgrow legacy platforms

notes.thesis: Defense TAM $1T+ locked in with bipartisan support. Taiwan tensions and Ukraine validation drive autonomous systems specifically. Backlogs of $526B combined for the primes provide unprecedented visibility. AVAV/KTOS represent the AI-defense intersection growing fastest.
caveats: Political risk if defense spending becomes a budget cut target.
Primes are slow-growth (single-digit revenue) but high-quality. Multiple compression possible.
Drone names (AVAV) trade on news flow — high vol.
Supply chain bottlenecks (semis for guidance, rare earths for magnets) create execution risk.

notes.headline: Storage Supercycle — PSTG, NTAP all-flash; STX HAMR archive; AI training data 40%+ CAGR.

all_flash.label: All-Flash Enterprise
all_flash.thesis: PSTG Q1 2026 >$1.06B (+20% YoY), Everpure rebrand reflects AI-first positioning. NTAP AIDE AI Data Engine co-engineered with NVIDIA. AI training data storage growing 40%+ CAGR.

hdd_archive.label: HDD / Cold Storage
hdd_archive.thesis: Seagate HAMR 40TB+ drives, stock +210% in 2025. Cold storage TAM $50B+ by 2030 — AI archives are massive.

nand_flash.label: NAND Flash
nand_flash.thesis: Newly independent post-WD spinoff. NAND pricing +20% Q4 2025. $42B contractual revenue backlog.

lead_lag.horizon: 5-7 years as AI training data demand outpaces traditional enterprise growth
lead_lag.chain_flow: AI model training → unprecedented data ingestion → all-flash for active + HDD for archive → NAND/HDD pricing power

notes.thesis: AI training and inference workloads have created a new storage tier above enterprise. PSTG is the breakout pure-play. STX HAMR is the archival angle (massive). NAND prices have power through 2027 on supply constraints.
caveats: Storage has historically been commoditized — pricing power requires constant innovation.
Hyperscalers building custom storage stacks bypasses traditional vendors.
STX +210% in 2025 means significant gains already priced in.
SNDK has limited price history as newly independent.

notes.headline: Robotics / Embodied AI — ABB, ROK, ISRG, TER: $4B → $61B by 2034 (31% CAGR).

industrial_robotics.label: Industrial Robotics & Automation
industrial_robotics.thesis: ABB Omniverse partnership (March 2026), 99% sim-to-reality fidelity, RobotStudio HyperReality. ROK industrial automation/control software with AI-driven predictive maintenance. Sim-to-reality validation is the inflection.

specialized_robotics.label: Specialized Robotics
specialized_robotics.thesis: ISRG da Vinci surgical robots with AI-guided planning. TER owns UR (collaborative arms) + MiR (warehouse bots) — autonomous robotics consolidation play.

lead_lag.horizon: 10+ year embodied AI buildout — long duration
lead_lag.chain_flow: AI foundation models → sim-to-reality validation → industrial robot deployment → labor displacement TAM expansion

notes.thesis: Embodied AI TAM grows from $4.1B to $61B by 2034 (31% CAGR). ABB-NVIDIA partnership validates feasibility. The technology inflection is the sim-to-reality fidelity hitting 99%. Industrial robotics (ABB) and collaborative/autonomous (TER UR/MiR) are consolidating around AI platforms.
caveats: Long-duration story — execution lags beyond typical momentum horizons.
Humanoid robotics (Tesla Optimus, Figure) is the wildcard that could disrupt the incumbents.
ISRG is more healthcare cycle than AI cycle.
Multiples are already pricing in significant adoption — disappointment risk high.

notes.headline: HBM & Advanced Packaging — MU + AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, ASML: 40% CAGR through 2028.

hbm_producers.label: HBM Producers (US-listed)
hbm_producers.thesis: MU HBM TAM 40% CAGR through 2028 ($35B → $100B). Hiroshima greenfield 2028 output. SK Hynix has the largest HBM share but Korea-listed; Samsung the same. MU is the only clean US-listed HBM play.

wfe_majors.label: Wafer Fab Equipment Majors
wfe_majors.thesis: AMAT etch/deposition 42% WFE share expansion, HBM tools 12+ month backlog. LRCX advanced packaging revenue tripled to $3B+. KLAC process control inspection/metrology critical for HBM yield.

specialty_equipment.label: Specialty Equipment
specialty_equipment.thesis: ONTO planarization/polishing HBM tools, +30% CAGR. ACMR China-exposed wet processing (geopolitical risk).

lithography.label: Lithography
lithography.thesis: Q1 2026 EUR 8.8B sales. EUV monopoly. Hybrid bonding equipment in development for advanced packaging.

lead_lag.horizon: 3-5 year buildout cycle with 12+ month equipment backlogs providing visibility
lead_lag.chain_flow: NVDA Blackwell ramp → HBM constraint → MU/SK Hynix capex → AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/ASML order books → 2028 capacity

notes.thesis: HBM is the single most supply-constrained node in AI infrastructure. SK Hynix capacity is locked through 2027. MU is the only US-listed HBM pure-play. Equipment suppliers (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, ASML) get the capex spend with 3-year backlog visibility — historically the highest-quality way to play semi cycles.
caveats: MU has historically been a cyclical name — valuation can compress quickly when HBM ASPs roll.
ASML has China export restrictions affecting EUV sales.
ACMR is China-exposed — geopolitical risk.
Hybrid bonding adoption timing affects ASML/AMAT incremental revenue.

notes.headline: Macro Supercycle Context — $725B hyperscaler capex (+77%), 1.2% US GDP, electrification 1920s analogue.

hyperscaler_capex_2026.comparison: Exceeds telecom buildout (1.0% GDP), trails railroad (6.0% GDP)

historical_analogies.railroads_1880s: Infrastructure phase 2024-2026 = railroad buildout. Consolidation/bankruptcy phase 2028-2035. Equipment suppliers (AMAT, ETN, VRT) win mid-term; operators (hyperscalers) win 50-yr long-term. Many stranded assets become essential decades later.
historical_analogies.electrification_1920s: Closest current analogue. Grid buildout 1920s = power infrastructure 2024-2026. Excess capacity risk 2026-2027. Resolution 1950s = AI productivity boom 2035-2040 justifies capex. Suppliers durability HIGH; capex cycle longer than railroads.
historical_analogies.fiber_telecom_late_1990s: Fiber overbuild 2000-2001 = DC capex 2024-2026 risk parallel. Stranded assets (Global Crossing) became essential broadband decades later. Equipment winners (CIENA, JDSU) > carriers (bankruptcy). For AI: AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/ASML/ETN > hyperscaler operators in 2028+ margin compression scenarios.
historical_analogies.china_commodity_2000s: Urbanization 2000s = AI infrastructure 2026-2030. Commodities then: iron ore/steel/coal/oil. Now: copper/lithium/nickel/uranium. Supply winners durable 8-12 years. Spot copper $14.5K → $20K+ consensus 2028-2029.

notes.thesis: We are in Phase 2 of an AI-driven supercycle most closely analogous to electrification of the 1920s. Hyperscaler capex of $725B (+77% YoY) at 1.2% of US GDP is unprecedented in modern history outside of WWII mobilization. Equipment suppliers and bottleneck-node owners (HBM, optics, power, cooling) carry the highest-quality earnings visibility through 2028. Hyperscalers themselves face a capex-to-revenue conversion risk by 2028-2029 if AI monetization disappoints.
key_signals_to_watch: Quarterly hyperscaler capex guidance — any cut = supercycle topping signal
NVDA forward gross margin trajectory — compression = ASIC competition real
HBM ASP trends in MU earnings — declining = supply catching up
Sovereign AI deal announcements — pipeline of $300B+ over 2026-2030
Power interconnection queue clearing — bottleneck for entire chain
caveats: Capex-to-revenue gap is the existential question. Closing it = supercycle extends. Failing = 2028 cliff.
Historical analogies all show 30-50% drawdowns mid-cycle even when long-term thesis was correct.
Geopolitical disruption (Taiwan, US-China decoupling) could fragment the global supply chain rapidly.
Open-source models (LLAMA, etc.) commoditize the model layer — winners shift from creators to deployers.

notes.headline: Server/Rack Integration Layer — SMCI, DELL, ANET: the missing layer between chip and cloud that assembles the actual racks.
notes.thesis: Between chip (NVDA/AVGO) and cloud (hyperscalers) sits the rack integration layer. Arista (ANET) is the Tier 1 switching fabric play — its 400G/800G Ethernet switches are in every major AI cluster. DELL is the OEM beneficiary with PowerEdge GPU servers. SMCI (Super Micro) is the pure-play liquid-cooled server design house — closest to the AI rack build — but has had accounting/audit issues (10-K delays, Hindenburg short report). SMCI is only tradeable once accounting credibility is restored. ANET is the cleanest name: recurring software (EOS), hyperscaler stickiness, no controversy.

lead_lag.horizon: 1-2 years alongside the rack buildout cycle
lead_lag.rationale: ANET leads because networking infrastructure gets ordered before servers ship. DELL lags because server OEM margins are thin and timing is lumpy. SMCI is uninvestable until audit completion.

caveats: SMCI: do not size until FY2024 10-K is filed and auditor concern resolved. Prior Hindenburg allegations of accounting irregularities.
ANET valuation is rich — trades at premium to software comps on hardware revenue. Multiple compression risk if hyperscaler capex guidance disappoints.
DELL has PC/commercial business drag — only ~20% of revenue is ISG (AI servers). Blended multiple stays depressed.

notes.headline: Nuclear Sub-Chain — CEG, NNE, OKLO, SMR, CCJ: AI power demand driving the next nuclear buildout cycle.

lead_lag.horizon: 3-7 years for SMR construction; 1-2 years for uranium supply response
lead_lag.rationale: CEG (Constellation Energy) is the only near-term play — existing nuclear fleet restart (Three Mile Island Unit 1 for Microsoft). CCJ (Cameco) is the uranium supply proxy — orders today, fuel in 2-3 years. NNE/OKLO/SMR are SMR pure-plays on a 5-10 year timeline — momentum/narrative now, revenue later.

existing_fleet.thesis: Restart and life-extension of existing nuclear plants. CEG restarted Three Mile Island Unit 1 for MSFT. VST has Comanche Peak. These are the only near-term AI power solutions that don't require new construction.

uranium_supply.thesis: Uranium spot price proxy. CCJ is the blue chip. URA is the ETF. UUUU (Energy Fuels) is US domestic production — strategic given Russia import ban. Any nuclear buildout announcement drives this basket.

smr_pure_plays.thesis: Small Modular Reactor companies. NNE (NuScale) is the furthest along in NRC licensing. OKLO is Sam Altman-backed, early stage. SMR (Nuscale spinoff). These are 5-10 year stories trading on narrative momentum. Size accordingly.

notes.thesis: All four hyperscalers said 'power constrained' in Q1 2026 earnings. The only 24/7 carbon-free baseload solution is nuclear. CEG/VST are near-term plays (existing fleet). CCJ is the supply chain anchor. NNE/OKLO/SMR are long-duration options. The key catalyst is data center power purchase agreements (PPAs) — each new nuclear PPA announcement re-rates the entire basket.
caveats: SMR pure-plays have no revenue — pure narrative. Drawdowns of 50-80% are possible without a fundamental change.
Uranium prices are volatile and tied to geopolitics (Kazakhstan, Russia supply disruptions).
NRC licensing timelines are unpredictable — NNE already had one project cancellation.
This chain trades differently from the chip/rack/optics chains — longer duration, higher vol, sentiment-driven.

notes.headline: Sovereign AI — UAE ($1.4T deal), Saudi HUMAIN, Japan, India: new NVDA demand leg outside US hyperscalers that changes the supply/demand equation.
notes.thesis: The AI buildout is no longer a US hyperscaler story. Sovereign AI programs are emerging as a distinct demand leg: UAE signed a $1.4T AI investment framework with the US (May 2026), Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN entity is ordering NVDA at scale, Japan committed $67B to domestic AI infra, India's government-backed AI mission is procuring GPUs for national compute. Each sovereign program needs the full stack — GPUs (NVDA), custom silicon (AVGO), interconnects (ALAB/CRDO), power (VRT/GEV), and neocloud infrastructure (NBIS for European sovereign). This demand is on top of, not instead of, US hyperscaler capex. NBIS (Nebius) is the cleanest pure-play on European/non-US sovereign AI cloud — Russian-origin company (formerly Yandex) that relocated to Netherlands, now building GPU cloud for EU sovereign clients.

lead_lag.horizon: 1-3 years as sovereign programs scale from announcement to deployment
lead_lag.rationale: NVDA gets the GPU orders first — sovereign deals are announced as GPU procurement agreements. Then the rack integration, interconnects, and cloud layers follow. NBIS is the read-through for non-US sovereign cloud.

key_events.UAE: $1.4T AI investment framework signed May 2026 — G42 and other UAE entities ordering NVDA H100/B200 at scale
key_events.Saudi_HUMAIN: Saudi Aramco / PIF-backed HUMAIN AI entity — committed to building national AI infrastructure
key_events.Japan: $67B government AI infrastructure program — domestic GPU procurement
key_events.India: IndiaAI Mission — government-subsidized GPU cloud access for startups and research

caveats: Export control risk: any tightening of AI chip export rules to Middle East/Asia would directly impair this demand leg.
Announcement vs. execution gap — sovereign programs move slowly from commitment to actual hardware delivery.
Geopolitical sensitivity: UAE/Saudi programs involve US government approval. Regime change or diplomatic friction could cancel deals.
NBIS is a small-cap ($3-5B) with thin US float and European listing — vol is high.
notes.source: ThemePulse value chain audit + public deal announcements — May 7, 2026

notes.headline: AI Inference & Edge Layer — ARM, QCOM, NVDA Jetson: as AI shifts from training to inference, the chip mix and winners change.
notes.thesis: The AI buildout has two phases: training (build the model — needs massive GPU clusters, NVDA's core market) and inference (run the model — broader architecture competition). Inference is growing faster than training spend, and the optimal chip for inference is NOT always a GPU. ARM architecture dominates inference at the edge — every smartphone, every laptop, every IoT device runs ARM. QCOM's Snapdragon X Elite with NPU is the PC inference play. Apple Silicon (M4/A18) is the gold standard for on-device inference but AAPL doesn't sell the chip. The inflection: as inference moves to the edge (on-device, not cloud), NVDA's share of inference workloads is threatened. This is a 2-3 year transition, not immediate.

lead_lag.horizon: 2-3 years for on-device inference to become a meaningful workload shift
lead_lag.rationale: ARM licenses its architecture to everyone — every inference chip (QCOM, Apple, MediaTek, Ampere cloud) runs ARM ISA. ARM royalties compound as inference scales. QCOM is the most direct AI PC/edge pure-play. NVDA's inference exposure is primarily data center inference (NIM microservices on H100/B200) — not edge.

architecture_map.cloud_inference: NVDA H100/B200 + NIM, AVGO custom ASICs, AWS Inferentia
architecture_map.edge_inference: ARM Cortex-X / Neoverse, QCOM Snapdragon NPU, Apple ANE

caveats: ARM trades at 70-80x forward earnings — enormous multiple. Any inference growth slowdown or NVDA competition is punishing.
QCOM has a smartphone cyclical overhang — AI PC momentum needs to outrun handset weakness.
NVDA is not standing still — Grace Blackwell (CPU+GPU) and Jetson Orin target edge inference directly.
On-device inference is primarily a consumer story — different catalysts than enterprise AI capex cycle.

notes.headline: Earnings Read-Through Map — which print moves which chain stocks the next session.

NVDA_earnings.thesis: NVDA is the mothership. Beat + raised guidance lifts entire AI semi chain. Miss/guide-down hits everything. Watch data center revenue and Blackwell ramp commentary specifically.

hyperscaler_capex.trigger: MSFT / META / AMZN / GOOGL quarterly earnings
hyperscaler_capex.thesis: Hyperscaler capex guidance is the second most important read-through in AI. All four said 'power and compute constrained' in Q1 2026 — that was a bullish read-through for VRT/GEV/ALAB. Any capex cut or 'pausing to digest' language is the biggest risk to the chain.

AVGO_earnings.thesis: AVGO's custom ASIC (XPU) commentary directly sets expectations for the custom silicon market. Strong XPU revenue = hyperscalers spending on non-NVDA AI chips = bullish for custom silicon ecosystem.

MU_earnings.thesis: MU's HBM pricing and demand commentary sets the memory supply/demand narrative. HBM ASP trends are the key — rising ASPs = supply-constrained = bullish.

ANET_earnings.thesis: ANET's AI cluster networking orders are the leading indicator for the rack integration build timeline. Product order book and backlog are the key metrics.

VRT_earnings.thesis: VRT's backlog commentary confirms or denies the power infrastructure demand thesis. Book-to-bill > 1.0 = constrained, bullish for the power chain.

CRWD_earnings.thesis: CRWD is the cybersecurity RS leader. Its ARR growth and platform consolidation commentary sets the tone for the sector. Falcon platform expansion drives competitive displacement read-through.

notes.thesis: Earnings read-throughs are the fastest way to get edge on positioning. Know which print moves which chain BEFORE the report, not after. The highest-alpha setup: if NVDA guides up strongly, buy ALAB/CRDO/MU pre-open the next day before consensus catches up. If hyperscalers cut capex, short VRT/GEV before the sector reprices.
caveats: Read-throughs are noisy — the market sometimes ignores them or reverses within 2-3 sessions.
Same-day options activity can front-run read-throughs — check unusual options flow in the chain names ahead of earnings.
Macro selloffs (rate fears, tariff news) can override sector-specific read-throughs entirely.

notes.headline: AI Ecosystem Layer Map — 6-layer value chain from memory → chip → interconnect → cybersecurity → power, with tier rankings and lead-lag flow.

memory.label: Memory Layer
memory.thesis: HBM3e is the real story — NVDA H100/B200 racks are HBM-constrained. MU is the cleanest US-listed play. SNDK is fresh IPO with massive NAND backlog ($42B contractual revenue) but less price history. SK Hynix and Samsung not cleanly tradeable in US accounts.
memory.catalyst: Any NVDA rack demand print lifts HBM suppliers directly.

neocloud.label: Neocloud Layer
neocloud.thesis: CoreWeave (CRWV) is a real GPU cloud business but debt-heavy post-IPO. NBIS (Nebius) is European AI cloud, thin float. IREN and Cipher are crypto miners pivoting to AI HPC — narrative-driven, not fundamentals. Watch IREN for execution proof points.
neocloud.catalyst: Hyperscaler capacity constraints driving GPU cloud demand; any DC contract announcements.

ai_chip.label: AI Chip Layer
ai_chip.thesis: NVDA is the irreplaceable GPU monopoly — the backbone of every layer below. AVGO owns custom ASIC (XPU) for hyperscalers (Google TPU, Meta MTIA, custom) — recurring revenue moat with 3-year design win visibility. MRVL recovering with custom silicon wins. INTC is a turnaround, not a momentum name. SMIC is geopolitically uninvestable for US accounts.
ai_chip.catalyst: NVDA Blackwell/Rubin ramp; hyperscaler capex prints confirming custom ASIC spend.

cybersecurity.label: Cybersecurity (Edge AI) Layer
cybersecurity.thesis: AI expanding the attack surface is the structural tailwind — more endpoints, more agentic processes, more LLM API exposure. CRWD is the RS leader with platform consolidation story. PANW is the enterprise incumbent with AI Copilot integration. NET (Cloudflare) bridges into AI gateway/inference. RBRK (data resilience) and CYBR (privileged access) are solid growers.
cybersecurity.catalyst: AI-driven breach headlines; platform consolidation deals; CRWD earnings prints.

interconnects_optics.label: AI Interconnects & Optics Layer
interconnects_optics.thesis: Direct NVDA rack-scale beneficiaries. ALAB (Astera Labs) makes PCIe/CXL retimers — every GB200 NVL72 rack needs them. CRDO (Credo) makes high-speed SerDes for switch fabrics. LITE (Lumentum) is optical components — real business but lumpier demand. Goldman Sachs called optical networking TAM 9x to $154B with CPO alone at $91B (142% CAGR 2024-2030).
interconnects_optics.catalyst: Co-packaged optics (CPO) adoption timeline; NVDA rack shipment velocity; any hyperscaler optical spend disclosure.

power_infra.label: Power-Infra Layer
power_infra.thesis: Every watt of AI compute needs power and cooling. VRT (thermal management / liquid cooling) and GEV (grid transformers / power equipment) are picks-and-shovels with multi-year backlogs — all four hyperscalers said 'power and compute constrained' in Q1 2026 earnings. VST is the nuclear/baseload angle. BE (Bloom Energy fuel cells) doesn't have the same demand clarity.
power_infra.catalyst: Hyperscaler data center build announcements; grid interconnection approvals; nuclear policy tailwinds.

lead_lag.chain_flow: NVDA demand signal → HBM constraint (MU) → custom ASIC ramp (AVGO/MRVL) → rack interconnects (ALAB/CRDO) → power/cooling bottleneck (VRT/GEV) → cybersecurity expansion (CRWD/PANW)
lead_lag.horizon: Structural 2-3 year buildout; momentum setups reset on each earnings cycle

notes.thesis: The AI buildout is a 6-layer physical stack, not a software story. The highest-conviction chain is NVDA → AVGO → ALAB → VRT: GPU demand drives custom ASIC (AVGO), which demands rack-scale interconnects (ALAB), which requires massive power infrastructure (VRT). All four have clean fundamentals and price action. Memory (MU) is a parallel high-conviction play as HBM remains supply-constrained. Cybersecurity is a secular winner but one layer removed from the core capex cycle. Neocloud names (CRWV, IREN) are narrative-first — require earnings execution proof before sizing up.
caveats: NVDA export restrictions (China) remain an overhang — any escalation hits the whole chain.
Custom ASIC (AVGO/MRVL) could displace NVDA share at the margin over 3-5 years — watch hyperscaler GPU mix commentary.

notes.headline: Photonics start-to-finish: bottlenecks are NOT raw materials — they're conversion, assembly, and test (low-fungibility, high-yield-curve steps)

supply_chain_steps.name: Mining / smelting / refining (indium)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: BYPRODUCT COUPLING — indium recovered from zinc residues, not primary mining; many zinc producers lack indium circuits. China refines ~68% of global primary indium. Geopolitical/policy choke point at refining stage.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Geological abundance high; industrial recovery + purification is the limit. Optical-grade purity adds another tier.

supply_chain_steps.name: InP substrate (crystal growth + wafering)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: WAFER-SIZE GAP vs Si CMOS. Historical 2-4 inch; transition to 6-inch is a multi-year qualification across the entire downstream stack (epi susceptors, lithography chucks, dicing). Brittleness + warp/TTV control.

tickers.role: 6-inch InP scalable wafer fab announced (laser sources for AI transceivers)

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Sumitomo Electric (5802.T) is the dominant InP substrate maker — not US-listed.

supply_chain_steps.name: Epitaxial growth (MOCVD / MBE)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: ATOMIC-SCALE PROCESS IP — proprietary recipes, specialized tooling, hazardous precursor chemistries. Low fungibility; concentrated among captive fabs + a few specialty epi houses.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: IQE plc (IQE.L) is the dominant external epi house but London-listed.

supply_chain_steps.name: Wafer fabrication (photonics front+back end)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: PROCESS COMPLEXITY — InP PIC flow can involve 243+ steps. Sidewall roughness, etch-depth precision, gold metallization (NOT shareable with Si CMOS lines). Defect density drives yield = cost-per-good-die.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: InP fab yields historically lag silicon CMOS — disclosed indirectly via gross margin trends.

supply_chain_steps.name: Dicing, test, yield
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: TEST THROUGHPUT — optical test slower than CMOS electrical probing (fiber alignment + power measurement). InP brittleness raises edge-defect risk. Test capacity gates shipments during demand surges.

tickers.role: Optical burn-in test systems (FOX-NP for photonic ICs)
Plasma etch chemistry, vacuum, photonics process control

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: AEHR is the most levered to AI-photonics test specifically (FOX-NP for VCSEL/PIC burn-in).

supply_chain_steps.name: Component assembly + hermetic packaging
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: PRECISION ALIGNMENT — single-mode fiber requires <1 µm tolerance with active alignment under live optical monitoring. Hermetic sealing (laser welding, He leak test) is throughput-limited. Hermetic package/Kovar/feedthrough supply gates final shipment AFTER most cost is incurred.

tickers.role: Fabrinet — contract manufacturer for optical assembly + hermetic packaging at scale
tickers.exposure: DIRECT — captures per-unit assembly fee for most major OEMs (COHR/LITE/CIEN/NVDA optical engines)

tickers.role: Jabil — high-volume electronics + optical module assembly

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Hermetic ceramic/Kovar housing supply is a hidden choke point — niche specialty suppliers, not publicly tracked.

supply_chain_steps.name: Transceiver module (optics + high-speed electronics)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: SYSTEM TEST + DSP integration — coherent test time + multi-temperature calibration. Module test capacity gates shipments even when die supply exists.
supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: Coherent (COHR) is the broadest single bet — substrates + epi + PIC + module all in-house.

supply_chain_steps.name: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO)
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: RELOCATION OF BOTTLENECKS — optical engines move into the same package as switch ASIC/GPU. Yield coupling: an optical fail scraps an expensive electronic package. Test access constrained, fiber attach must survive reflow profiles. Bottleneck migrates from module final test → wafer-level/package-level test + fiber attach.

tickers.role: Silicon photonics foundry for CPO partners
Switch ASIC + co-packaged optics (Tomahawk 5/6 + CPO variants)
Spectrum-X/NVLink CPO roadmap (silicon photonics inside switches)

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: CPO doesn't shrink the supply chain — it shifts where the value/risk concentrates (advanced packaging, test, fiber attach).

supply_chain_steps.name: Fiber + connector deployment
supply_chain_steps.bottleneck: FIBER PURITY + CONNECTOR PRECISION — preforms with ppb impurity levels, draw control. Single-mode fiber MFD ~9 µm with attenuation targets ≤0.4 dB/km. Connectorization, ferrule polishing, cleaning regimes scale with rack/row fiber count.

tickers.role: Corning — dominant single-mode fiber maker + bare fiber + connectors

supply_chain_steps.key_caveat: AI rack architecture (GPU-scale fabrics) raises fiber count per rack — shifts value to bulk fiber/jumper supply.

highest_margin_choke_points: Test capacity (AEHR / COHU / CAMT / ONTO / KEYS) — gates shipments, hard to scale fast
Hermetic packaging + alignment (FN as the scale player) — late-stage gate, high inventory cost if blocked
InP substrates at 6-inch (COHR / AXTI) — first-mover wins multi-year qualification cycle
Vertically integrated photonics (COHR) — captures end-to-end value from substrate to module
highest_demand_pull: AVGO + NVDA force CPO TAM into existence by integrating optics into their packages
Hyperscalers (per linked notes) commit multi-year contracts ⇒ supply gets pre-booked
structural_winners: FN (Fabrinet) — every transceiver assembled at scale passes through them; pricing power as bottleneck
COHR — only US-listed name with substrate + epi + PIC + module all in-house
AEHR — only pure-play optical burn-in test maker; AI photonics ramp = direct revenue
GLW — fiber demand scales with rack fiber count; AI cluster builds raise per-rack fiber count materially
structural_risks: AAOI / pluggable specialists — CPO long-term threatens pluggable TAM
Pure-play silicon photonics (POET) — execution risk if heterogeneous integration timeline slips
Indium price-spike risk → all InP-dependent margins compress in unison

lead_lag.horizon: 2026-2028 multi-year
lead_lag.rationale: Hyperscaler/integrator capex commitments (per linked notes) flow downstream through multi-year photonics ramps. Substrate scaling alone is a 2-4 year cycle. Photonics suppliers benefit on a 1-4Q lag from each capex commitment milestone.

trade_setup: Pure-play test bench: AEHR + ONTO + CAMT — gate function for AI photonics ramp; LRCX/AMAT may not capture this since it's test/inspection not deposition.
Vertically integrated photonics: COHR — substrates + epi + PIC + module + 6-inch InP fab announced. Best single-name expression.
Fabrinet (FN) — the assembly bottleneck owner. Scales with whoever wins downstream module share.
GLW — fiber + connector volumes scale with rack fiber count, less cyclical than module ASPs.
Pair: long FN/COHR/AEHR vs short pluggable-only specialists (AAOI) on CPO transition risk.
caveats: Foreign tickers (5802.T Sumitomo Electric, IQE.L IQE plc) are the dominant external substrate/epi suppliers — not in FMP live feed.
Hermetic packaging suppliers are mostly private/niche — opportunity but not directly tradeable.
InP yield trajectory rarely disclosed; infer from gross margin trends in COHR/LITE quarterlies.
CPO economics depend on advanced-packaging cost curves at TSMC/Intel — supply chain risk if packaging capacity slips.
Indium price/supply shock would compress margins across all InP names simultaneously; consider as systemic risk, not idiosyncratic.

notes.headline: SIVE (Sivers Semiconductors) likely Apple silicon-photonics supplier — undiscovered alpha on a foreign-listed name

notes.headline: AI infra state of play: Energy = primary conviction · copper-to-optics = highest-conviction networking · Memory = secular not cyclical

subtheses.title: AI Energy is the primary conviction play
subtheses.argument: Power is THE defining constraint of the AI buildout, not compute. Hyperscalers acknowledged 'power-and-compute constrained' in unison; compute side has visible relief paths (CoWoS expansion, foundry capex, custom silicon). Power side is structurally bounded by permitting + interconnect + grid construction cycles measured in YEARS not quarters. Allocations rotating beyond accelerators/networking into the energy stack.
trade_setup: BE — on-site fuel cells bypass interconnect queue; relief-valve trade with shorter timeline than IPP/nuclear
GEV — grid equipment (transformers, switchgear) front-runs IPP capex
VRT — datacenter cooling + power conditioning; structural beneficiary of high-density AI racks
IREN — 'power-secured site' compute play (neocloud overlap with energy thesis — they own the substations)
subtheses.extension_note: Reframes the prior 'EARLY cycle phase' read on Power as structurally MORE important than compute — not just earlier in the cycle but a bigger pool of capital.

subtheses.title: Copper-to-optics is the highest-conviction networking theme
subtheses.argument: At 800G+ lane rates, copper interconnect loss + retiming complexity hits a wall. Silicon photonics, EML (externally modulated laser) lasers, and co-packaged optics are the only path forward. Most investors can't name the names — that's where the alpha is. Multi-year transition because every hyperscaler design needs to qualify the new optical engines.
speculative_picks: SIVE-B.ST (Sivers Semiconductors) — Stockholm-listed silicon-photonics alpha, see sive-apple-silicon-photonics note
IQE.L (IQE plc) — London-listed dominant external epi house for compound semis; not US-tradeable but strategically critical
subtheses.extension_note: Sharpens the prior photonics thesis: the COPPER → OPTICS transition itself is the alpha, not just the test/inspection bottleneck. EML lasers + silicon photonics are the secular shift.

subtheses.title: AI Memory is no longer cyclical — it's secular
subtheses.argument: Samsung disclosed 2027 demand pre-booked. SNDK Q3 print: 78% GM, $11B in customer financial guarantees. Today's signal: supply constrained through 2028 (extending Samsung's 2027 read by another year). Demand accelerating faster than any model projected. The historical NAND/DRAM cycle (peak → reversion → trough → recovery) is broken because AI inference creates a permanent floor on demand that doesn't unwind on a price reset.
subtheses.extension_note: Updates the horizon from 'multi-year' to 'through 2028.' The structural reframing matters for valuation — secular memory deserves a tech-platform multiple, not a cyclical commodity multiple. MU/SNDK should re-rate higher when the market accepts this.

trade_setup_summary: REWEIGHT: shift conviction from compute-side (NVDA/AVGO/etc) toward energy-side (BE/GEV/VRT/IREN). Compute has relief paths; power is structurally bounded.
ADD: photonics secular winners (LITE/AAOI/COHR/FN/AEHR) on copper→optics transition. Sub-bench: POET/TSEM/MTSI as architectural alpha.
EXTEND HOLD: memory cohort (MU/SNDK) into 2027-2028. Don't trim on cycle-peak fears — the cycle is broken.
WATCH: SIVE (foreign) for silicon photonics confirmation; signs of widespread CPO adoption in 2026 H2.
caveats: Energy thesis kill: AI ROI miss → hyperscaler capex pulled back → power demand assumptions cut. Watch META/MSFT capex guides.
Copper-to-optics kill: CPO timeline slips by 12+ months (qualification or yield issues). AAOI most exposed if pluggable TAM compresses faster than expected.
Memory secular kill: hyperscaler concentration risk — $11B in SNDK guarantees from 3-5 customers. Bilateral risk.
All three theses share a common kill: AI infrastructure capex revision down.

notes.headline: Glass Substrate Value Chain — GLW/LRCX/ONTO/KLAC + Japanese specialists: AI packaging next frontier.

glass_materials.label: Glass Materials
glass_materials.thesis: Corning (GLW) is the dominant US player in specialty glass — borosilicate glass for substrates is a natural extension of their Display and Optical Physics segments. ASGLY (Asahi Glass / AGC, 5201.T) and NIDGY (Nippon Electric Glass, 5214.T) are the Japanese incumbents already supplying prototype glass panels to Intel, AMD, and TSMC packaging lines. Glass substrates offer 50% lower signal loss, 40% better flatness, and near-zero moisture absorption vs organic — enabling denser interconnect pitch at scale.

tgv_equipment.label: TGV Equipment (Through-Glass Via)
tgv_equipment.thesis: Lpkf Laser (LPK) makes the laser systems that drill Through-Glass Vias — the critical enabling step that allows vertical signal routing through glass panels. No TGV drilling = no glass substrate chip integration. LPKF is the pick-and-shovel play with the most direct exposure; their LIDE (Laser Induced Deep Etching) process is the leading TGV formation technology.

etching_systems.label: Etching & Patterning
etching_systems.thesis: Lam Research (LRCX) etching systems are required to pattern the fine-pitch redistribution layers on glass panels. Glass etching has tighter process windows than organic — favorable for Lam's high-selectivity etch tools. Incremental TAM expansion as glass substrate adoption scales into HVM.

dicing_equipment.label: Dicing Equipment
dicing_equipment.thesis: Disco Corp (DSCSY, 6146.T) is the world leader in dicing/grinding equipment. Glass panels are harder and more brittle than organic substrates — Disco's stealth dicing laser technology is the preferred singulation method. Direct beneficiary of glass substrate HVM ramp.

bonding_systems.label: Bonding Systems
bonding_systems.thesis: Shibaura Mechatronics (SMHSF) supplies precision bonding equipment used in the chip-to-glass attach process. Glass substrate's coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch with silicon requires tighter bonding tolerances — plays to Shibaura's high-precision equipment strengths.

inspection_tools.label: Inspection & Metrology
inspection_tools.thesis: Onto Innovation (ONTO) and KLA (KLAC) provide the inspection and metrology systems required to qualify glass substrate lines. Glass introduces new defect modes (micro-cracks, via sidewall roughness, CTE-driven warpage) that require new inspection recipes. Both are already name-dropped by substrate players as key qualification partners. ONTO is the higher-beta play; KLAC has the broadest moat across all inspection nodes.

lead_lag.horizon: 2026-2029 HVM ramp; Intel Glass Substrate roadmap targets 2028 volume production
lead_lag.chain_flow: Glass materials qualification → TGV drilling (LPK) → etching/patterning (LRCX) → dicing (DSCSY) → bonding (SMHSF) → inspection/metrology (ONTO/KLAC) → chip integration → hyperscaler adoption

notes.thesis: Glass substrates are the leading candidate to replace organic substrates for next-gen AI chip packaging — enabling higher interconnect density, lower signal loss, and better thermal stability at the cost of new process complexity. Intel's Glass Substrate program (targeting 2028 HVM) and AMD/TSMC exploratory programs have triggered named equipment qualifications across TGV drilling, etching, dicing, bonding, and inspection. The entire value chain was explicitly named dropped by industry participants — each layer has a clear pick-and-shovel beneficiary. TAM impact: advanced packaging substrate market grows from ~$12B (2024) to $28B+ (2030); glass captures an estimated 20-30% of that by 2030.
caveats: Glass substrate HVM is still 2028+ — near-term is qualification and prototype revenue, not volume.
CTE mismatch with silicon remains an unsolved yield challenge at scale.
Intel execution risk — their Glass Substrate program is the primary catalyst; delays push out the whole chain.
Japanese names (ASGLY, NIDGY, DSCSY, SMHSF) are thinly traded ADRs/OTC — illiquid, wide spreads.
Organic substrate incumbents (Ibiden, Shinko) are investing in glass as a hedge — competition risk.
LRCX and KLAC are large-cap diversified; glass substrate is incremental TAM, not a primary driver.
notes.source: Industry name-drops from glass substrate ecosystem participants — May 2026
